passage:
The morning market starts before sunrise. Sellers set up tables while most people are still sleeping. Fish, vegetables, fruit, flowers, and cooked food fill the narrow street.
Jenny visited the market with her father for a school report. She expected only noise and crowds. Instead, she noticed a kind of order. Sellers knew where to place things. Customers knew which stands opened earliest. People greeted each other by name.
Her father bought tomatoes from the same woman he had known for ten years.
Jenny wrote in her report that the market was not just a place to buy food. It was a place where time, work, and relationships met before breakfast.
